title: Flash flood
tldr: Move to higher ground immediately if a flash-flood warning affects you or water is rising. Never cross flowing water on foot or in a vehicle. Leave low areas, canyons and basements without waiting to see how high the water gets.
steps: Move away from streams, low roads and drainage channels.
Do not drive across a flooded road; the roadbed may be missing.
Call emergency services and move to a higher open level without becoming trapped in a closed attic.
Use current evacuation and road-closure instructions.
next: Wait for official clearance. Water may rise after rain stops or when storms occur upstream.
watch: A small-looking current can sweep away people and vehicles.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: Move uphill before the route fills; leave belongings behind. If trapped above floodwater, remain in a safe elevated position and signal your location. Do not attempt to swim a current or enter water to rescue property.
household: Plan a route that avoids low crossings and can be used by everyone. Carry children only within the helper’s real ability and do not attempt improvised water rescues. Know where the family will regroup on higher ground.
pack_now: Prioritize supplies named in this guide that are usable by the person who needs them. Keep the checklist and relevant contact details accessible. Check carrying capacity, storage and equipment instructions in advance; collecting equipment must not delay the immediate protective action.
faqs: Can I cross a shallow-looking road?

Do not enter moving or uncertain floodwater on foot or in a vehicle. Depth, current and road damage are difficult to assess from the surface. Choose another route or a safer higher location before the crossing becomes your only option.
A warning arrives while camping — now what?

Move out of low channels and drainage paths promptly when safe. Conditions upstream can change your location quickly even without local rain. Keep the group together and carry only essentials that do not delay the move.
scope: Civilian educational guidance. Linked references may use U.S. emergency systems; local warning methods, laws, services and conditions differ.
